title: Compliance: 44 Track Dystopia Music Pack
tagline: 44 dystopia music tracks for any game engine. A clock ticks until the player gets out.
description:
Compliance is a 44 track corporate dystopia music pack for any game engine: one megacorp building, from the welcome video to the fire exit.

It ships 38 full looping pieces and 6 short system cues as OGG and editable MIDI, royalty free for commercial games, with three full tracks free on this page.

What is inside

44 tracks · 38 loops of a minute or more · 6 cues · OGG + editable MIDI · 58:07

  • Five acts from the first day to the way out: Onboarding (8), The Floors (9), The Audit (9), The Purge (7) and Outside (5), plus 6 system cues: Access Granted, Access Denied, Incident Logged, Quota Met, Terminated and Security Alert.
  • The clock: a quiet side stick ticks on every beat of tracks 1 to 39 and stops at track 40, Service Tunnels, when the record leaves the building. It is its own part in the MIDI, so you can drop it and render your own.
  • The voice: choir and voice oohs sound only in the last 5 tracks. Until then the only voice on the record is a synth voice, and those last 5 tracks use no synth at all.
  • The decay: the harmony slows act by act, a new chord every bar, then every 2, 4 and 8 bars, then every bar again outside.
  • One seed theme, The Chime, in all 44 tracks, and five more for the working day, repetition, being watched, force and the way out.
  • Every full piece loops for at least a minute (the shortest loop is 62.2 seconds), with LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags in its OGG file.
  • 31 General MIDI instruments, among them electric piano, vibraphone, muted trumpet, clarinet, violin, cello, synth brass, sawtooth lead, synth voice, choir aahs and acoustic grand piano.

The theory and audio reports (788 and 510 checks, 0 failed) ship inside the download.

Every track in order: the ticks up to the door and the sung notes after it, read from the shipped MIDI.

Every full piece as a strip of chords on one time axis, with its loop length.

The score sheet: all 44 tracks, from Welcome to the Company to Exit Interview.

Works with

RPG Maker MV and MZ read the loop tags with no plugin. The Readme gives import steps for Godot 4 (followed in a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, all 44 files), Unity and GameMaker. Any engine that plays OGG can use the files, and the MIDI lets you score it with your own sounds.

Try it free

Three full tracks with their MIDI are free on this page: The Atrium (a new chord every bar), The Chairman, the final boss (a new chord every eight bars), and Daylight (no clock, voices, chords moving every bar again). More free tracks from our other albums: Overture, the free sampler.

Licence and how it was made

Royalty free for commercial games, no credit required. Do not resell the tracks as music assets. Every track is composed in code and rendered through a General MIDI soundfont; no generative audio model was used. The code and the cover art were made with AI tools. Every tune was composed for this record; no game, book or film cue is quoted.

Versions

v1.0 (30 October 2026): first release, 44 tracks.

devlog.title: Compliance is out: a 44 track corporate dystopia score with a clock that stops at the door
devlog.body:
Compliance is a 44 track music pack for games set inside a megacorp: one building from the welcome video through the floors, the audit and the purge to the fire exit, plus 6 short system cues. It is live now, $9.99, with three full tracks free on the page.

The idea. A quiet side stick ticks on every beat of tracks 1 to 39, 4564 ticks in all, and stops at track 40, when the record leaves the building. Choir and voice oohs sound only after that point; until then the only voice is a synth voice. The harmony slows act by act, a new chord every bar, then every 2, 4 and 8 bars, then every bar again outside.

How it was checked. 788 theory checks and 510 audio checks, 0 failed, with the reports inside the download. The clock, the voice, the chord lengths and the loop tags were each measured on the shipped files, and the loop tags were followed into a blank Godot 4.7.2 project.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render; the MIDI is there so you can move it to your own sounds, or drop the clock. No game, book or film cue is quoted. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model was used; the cover art was made with AI tools.
